# MCP Client - Spring AI and ChatGPT API

This example demonstrates how to use the
[Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro)
within a prompt when working with [ChatGPT](https://platform.openai.com/) via
its client API. In this case, a file-based MCP server is used, enabling users to
interact with the file system through text commands. While MCP shows
considerable promise, it also introduces significant security risks. For
example, a malicious user could potentially initiate harmful actions, and the
model may misinterpret a prompt and perform unintended operations, such as
deleting files.

MCP supplies the model with a list of available tools with every request, after
which the model decides whether to invoke any of them. These tool definitions
contribute to the overall prompt size, and an excessively large list can
negatively affect model performance. Rather than including all tools with every
request, it is preferable to restrict the toolset to those that are relevant to
the specific prompt.

This example uses [Spring AI](https://spring.io/projects/spring-ai), a
Java-based framework for building applications powered by large language models
(LLMs). It provides features such as prompt management, LLM call chaining,
memory handling, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)—which enhances responses
using external knowledge—and integration with external data sources, all within
the Java ecosystem.

[LangChain4J](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j) is an alternative
framework that also provides an abstraction layer between LLMs and the
application.

This example connects to OpenAI’s ChatGPT, which is hosted by OpenAI. An API
key, available from the OpenAI platform, is required.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [OpenAI API Key](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys)

-  Container runtime, such as [colima](https://github.com/abiosoft/colima) or
   [Podman](https://podman.io/)

## Run the example

1. OpenAI API Key

   If you have not already done so, please create an API key from
   [OpenAI API Key](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys).

   Verify that the OpenAI APIs can be successfully invoked. The following
   command assumes that the API key is stored at `~/.chatgpt/api.key`.

   ```shell
   curl https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions \
     --silent \
     --header "Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.chatgpt/api.key)" \
     --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data '{
     "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
     "messages": [
       {
         "role": "user",
         "content": "When did humans first land on the Moon?"
       }
     ],
     "temperature": 0.0
   }'
   ```

   The model response

   ```json
   {
     "id": "chatcmpl-DYahL1QgUzlDkNVAu8q5cLaQmNibm",
     "object": "chat.completion",
     "created": 3386752496,
     "model": "gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18",
     "choices": [
       {
         "index": 0,
         "message": {
           "role": "assistant",
           "content": "Humans first landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969, during NASA's Apollo 11 mission. Astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first and second humans to walk on the lunar surface, while Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit aboard the command module. Neil Armstrong famously declared, \"That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind,\" as he stepped onto the Moon.",
           "refusal": null,
           "annotations": []
         },
         "logprobs": null,
         "finish_reason": "stop"
       }
     ],
     "usage": {
       "prompt_tokens": 16,
       "completion_tokens": 87,
       "total_tokens": 103,
       "prompt_tokens_details": {
         "cached_tokens": 0,
         "audio_tokens": 0
       },
       "completion_tokens_details": {
         "reasoning_tokens": 0,
         "audio_tokens": 0,
         "accepted_prediction_tokens": 0,
         "rejected_prediction_tokens": 0
       }
     },
     "service_tier": "default",
     "system_fingerprint": "fp_43b64008fd"
   }
   ```

   This example makes use of the Spring framework. For security purposes and to
   prevent exposing the API key in documentation, the following commands assume
   the key is saved in the `.chatgpt/openai-api.yml` file within the user’s home
   directory.

   ```yaml
   spring:
     ai:
       openai:
         api-key: sk-proj-XXXXX
   ```

2. Build the application

   This step assumes that a valid OpenAI API Key is available at
   `~/.chatgpt/openai-api.yml`. See Step 1 for more information about how to do
   this.

   By default, the application starts the MCP filesystem server with `docker`.
   If you are using Podman without a Docker-compatible wrapper, set
   `MCP_CONTAINER_COMMAND=podman` when running Maven or the application.
   On SELinux-enabled systems, such as Oracle Linux, the bind-mounted `data`
   directory may also need relabeling. In that case, set
   `MCP_CONTAINER_MOUNT_SUFFIX=,relabel=shared`.
   The container image is fully qualified as
   `docker.io/mcp/rust-mcp-filesystem` so that Podman does not need
   interactive short-name resolution.

   ```shell
   podman pull docker.io/mcp/rust-mcp-filesystem

   MCP_CONTAINER_COMMAND=podman \
   MCP_CONTAINER_MOUNT_SUFFIX=,relabel=shared \
   ./mvnw clean verify
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the application was created.

   ```shell
   tree --prune --sort=name -L 1 './target'
   ```

   The application Fat JAR file

   ```
   ./target
   ├── mcp-client-springai-chatgpt-api-1.0.0.jar
   └── mcp-client-springai-chatgpt-api-1.0.0.jar.original

   1 directory, 2 files
   ```

3. Run the program

   This step assumes that a valid OpenAI API Key is available at
   `~/.chatgpt/openai-api.yml`. See Step 1 for more information about how to do
   this.

   Run the example with the default prompt.

   ```shell
   java \
     -jar './target/mcp-client-springai-chatgpt-api-1.0.0.jar'
   ```

   Although the prompt remains the same, the output may vary with each run.
